title: Brewster's Tab
statusNote: Timestamps follow the story's order and have not been checked against a subtitle file. Every dollar figure is a modelled estimate in 1985 dollars, built from the formulas in the ledger below.

events.label: Hackensack Bulls
events.detail: Monty Brewster pitches for a minor-league team and has no money.

events.label: Bailed out
events.detail: A stranger posts bail and drives Monty to Manhattan.

events.label: The will
events.detail: Great-uncle Rupert's terms: spend $30 million in 30 days and inherit $300 million. He can't own anything at the end.

events.label: Turns down the wimp clause
events.detail: Monty passes on a guaranteed $1 million and takes the challenge.

events.label: Day one walking money
events.detail: New clothes for Monty and Spike, and cash for the month.
calc: Cash for tips and nights out, per day

events.label: Luxury hotel suite
events.detail: A top-floor suite for the month, with room service.
calc: Suite and room service, per night

events.label: Office space
events.detail: A Manhattan floor on short notice. He can't buy it, so it's rent, plus rented furniture.
calc: Month's rent at a short-notice premium

events.label: Hiring spree
events.detail: Staff on generous salaries. The will allows wages as long as people do the work.

events.label: Limos and security
events.detail: Cars and guards on call around the clock.

events.label: The rare stamp
events.detail: He buys a rare stamp, then uses it to mail a postcard. This figure is a placeholder until the price is checked against the dialogue.

events.label: Redecorating
events.detail: The office is done over more than once.

events.label: Investments built to fail
events.detail: Long-shot ventures he picks because they should lose money.

events.label: Bulls vs. Yankees
events.detail: He pays for an exhibition game between his Bulls and the New York Yankees.

events.label: A sure loser wins
events.detail: One of the ventures pays off. The money comes back and the tab goes down.

events.label: Runs for mayor
events.detail: He starts a campaign telling New Yorkers to vote for None of the Above.

events.label: Fender-bender payoff
events.detail: After a minor car accident, Monty is the one who pays.

events.label: Ad blitz
events.detail: TV spots and billboards that tell people not to vote for anybody.
calc: Prime-time TV spots in New York

events.label: Another accidental profit
events.detail: More money comes back from a deal that was meant to lose.

events.label: Rallies and polling
events.detail: The campaign keeps spending while None of the Above climbs in the polls.

events.label: Drops out
events.detail: He might win, so he quits the race.

events.label: The big party
events.detail: One huge party for everyone he knows.

events.label: Settling every bill
events.detail: The film never shows this money being spent. It's whatever the itemized estimates leave short of $30 million.

events.label: The last few dollars
events.detail: With seconds to go, the last of the money goes out.
Thirty million gone in thirty days. The inheritance is his.
